answer: Each identity registers one pearl lot at a wharf custody house and locks a 70-credit bond. It files a kernel-signed chain, each transfer stamped at a wharf checkpoint with pearl count and weight. Auditors recompute it from the log: stamps must run in order and match the lot; a broken or duplicate link burns its bond. First fee 31, kth pays 31+6(k-1), 1000th 6025, so 1000 fakes pay 3028000 plus 70000 locked. An honest agent pays one fee and one bond, refunded after a clean epoch. A rented-lot ring fails because a borrowed pearl lot bears its owner's kernel chain, caught on recomputation.
